statement.excerpt: As I put it in earlier today on X, re a call for federal AI standards in lieu of state standards only makes sense if there are (sensible) federal standards, but Congress has not put anything serious forward to a vote.
statement.document_title: Mayday: The White House is attempting to circumvent Congress and crush the rights of individual states to regulate AI.

from_speaker: federal AI standards in lieu of state standards
Congress has not put anything serious forward to a vote
our_interpretation: The plain contextual reading concerns substantive federal AI safeguards that could provide a national alternative to state AI regulation.

A qualifying proposal would impose meaningful, cross-cutting obligations on AI developers or deployers. A framework covering high-impact systems or frontier models could qualify; it need not address every AI harm or expressly preempt state law.
A targeted intimate-imagery law, research funding, government procurement rules, or voluntary technical guidance alone would not satisfy that scope.

I interpret 'to a vote' as a vote before either full chamber, including a vote on qualifying provisions within a larger bill. Passage or enactment is not required. Marcus did not expressly exclude committee votes.

The period is cumulative through November 19, 2025. Its start is unspecified because 'has not' supplies no starting date. Legislative proceedings were publicly reportable immediately, so a quarterly reporting period would be inappropriate.
I treat 'serious' as substantive regulatory obligations, without judging whether Marcus would personally approve of them.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently complete review of legislative texts and chamber proceedings establishes that no qualifying federal AI safeguards were brought to a floor vote by November 19, 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An official record identifies at least one floor vote by November 19, 2025 on qualifying federal AI safeguards, whether those provisions passed or failed.

One qualifying floor vote would contradict the claim; a sufficiently comprehensive record showing none would support it under the stated reading.
